prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: Русский / Tiếng Việt · Diacritics (language ru).
Grid: 3 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Термин" · longest unbreakable word 134px · one-line width 134px
  col 2: header "Tiếng Việt" · longest unbreakable word 36px · one-line width 111px
  col 3: header "Описание" · longest unbreakable word 90px · one-line width 615px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 568px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 567px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"poor","why":"The Russian terms break within words, making the first column difficult to scan despite a generous description column."},"B":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Russian terms and Vietnamese phrases remain intact, while the descriptions have enough width to wrap naturally. The columns feel well balanced for their roles."},"C":{"grade":"good","why":"The Russian terms stay intact and descriptions read comfortably, though the narrow Vietnamese column splits two short phrases across lines."},"D":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Both term columns stay on one line, but they take space from the descriptions, which wrap into narrow blocks and make the rows taller."},"E":{"grade":"good","why":"The wide description column reads comfortably and Russian terms stay intact, but the narrow Vietnamese column splits two phrases across lines."},"F":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The description column is reasonably wide, but the Vietnamese phrases wrap awkwardly, leaving short final lines; the first column has more space than it needs."}},"best":["B"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"C and E are close: both trade Vietnamese phrase width for a wider description column."}
